A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same F2D2 research work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across additions and relocations.

before.justification: V2 reports original CIFAR-10, ImageNet-64, and checkerboard experiments, including likelihood and generation results, self-guidance evaluations, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: V3 retains those original results and adds CelebA-64 experiments and LSD-based checkerboard evaluations.

M1.justification: The joint flow map, shared backbone and divergence head, training objectives, and self-guidance procedure are retained. Lagrangian likelihood self-distillation was already derived in v2 Appendix A, Equations A.7–A.9; v3 supplies explicit pseudocode and experimental implementations of that existing branch.

E1.justification: V3 adds CelebA-64 face generation and likelihood evaluation while retaining CIFAR-10, ImageNet-64, and checkerboard coverage. It also adds checkerboard density evaluation on ground-truth data alongside the retained generated-sample visualization, providing a focused extension of the existing tasks.

E2.justification: Lagrangian self-distillation (LSD) becomes an evaluated comparator in the new CelebA-64 and checkerboard comparisons. Existing comparator sets remain intact, including the flow-matching and Shortcut checkerboard comparison relocated to Figure 5.

E3.justification: The added LSD experiments use unrestricted time-pair sampling, dedicated training budgets and batch allocations, and backward integration for the new checkerboard evaluation. Existing CIFAR-10/ImageNet metrics, evaluation samples, and forward-only Shortcut/MeanFlow settings are retained; these are additional protocols rather than revisions to the old experiments.

E4.justification: V3 adds a checkerboard diagnostic of backward likelihood evaluation on ground-truth data, comparing LSD-F2D2 with LSD and flow matching in Figure 6. The earlier generated-sample analysis survives as Figure 5, and the divergence-scaling, loss-weighting, and self-guidance ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the benchmark results. The Hutchinson estimator and its reported variance discussion are unchanged.

E6.justification: V3 adds a substantive result set validating the previously unevaluated Lagrangian branch: CelebA-64 NLL/FID, per-sample likelihood errors, and checkerboard findings. For example, Table 3 reports 8-step LSD-F2D2 NLL/FID of 1.64/2.41 versus LSD's -6.78/3.33. Existing CIFAR-10/ImageNet results are unchanged; these are new comparisons, not same-setting improvements over v2.

T1.justification: The joint-flow characterizations, Lagrangian/Eulerian/semigroup derivations, and Appendix B proofs are retained. Completing the diagonal velocity arguments in Equation A.9 and reminding readers that the Lagrangian limit covers the tangent condition clarify existing mathematics without introducing a substantive theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about modular joint acceleration, accurate few-step likelihoods, sample quality, and maximum-likelihood self-guidance. Replacing 'single model' with 'single flow map' is terminological; the additional experiments support existing claims.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanations, backward-approximation qualification, and interpretations of retained experiments remain unchanged. Appendix F preserves the same early-stopping, resource, unconditional-generation, scaling-sensitivity, and generalization limitations. The new LSD/CelebA passages add observations without a new explanatory mechanism or limitation.

D1.justification: Appendix C adds LSD/CelebA architecture, hardware, precision, training-budget, loss-scaling, and time-sampling details, plus explicit instantiation pseudocode. The reproducibility statement newly points readers to a website for PyTorch and JAX implementation links. Existing implementation descriptions are largely retained.

R1.justification: V3 adds the CelebA reference, Liu et al. (2015), and explicitly identifies the evaluated LSD instantiation with the already-cited Boffi et al. (2025a). The related-work discussion and broader novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Editing is localized: publication headers change, Algorithm 1 becomes a general recipe, instantiation pseudocode moves or expands in Appendix C, and experimental descriptions gain LSD/CelebA material. Most prose and the section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: The original checkerboard Figure 3 moves to Figure 5 with a more specific caption; a new LSD display shares the main-text page with the CelebA table. V3 adds backward-density plots, CelebA tables and galleries, and a hyperparameter-table column. Existing visual style and most displays remain intact.

improvement.justification: V3 strengthens empirical support for F2D2's modularity by testing the already-derived Lagrangian branch. CelebA results and per-sample errors, together with explicit backward-density checkerboard checks, broaden validation beyond v2's evidence. Added implementation details and code-access instructions also help reproducibility. These are useful incremental gains; the central framework, existing results, and acknowledged calibration limitations remain unchanged.
